summary.mechanism_note: Domain-retention/partner-driven-oligomerization, the best-characterized instance of the mechanism this benchmark's domain-retention framework is built around: EML4 contributes its N-terminal trimerization domain (TD, also called the HELP domain, historically described as a coiled-coil), which forces constitutive, ligand-independent self-association of the fused ALK intracellular kinase domain and drives trans-autophosphorylation. This substitutes for ALK's native ligand-induced extracellular-domain dimerization -- loss of that extracellular region is permissive (removes ALKAL1/ALKAL2 dependence) but the partner-driven oligomerization, not the loss itself, is the necessary activating event.
